items.title: 71231_Sam Wooding Oral History Interview
items.q: So later on he went with Fats Waller.

ctx.x: No, I played the Arcadia, I played the Arcadia here on Broadway. And we did fairly good for awhile, but first thing you know, we had to get out of that. After we left there -- we stayed there about three months, two months or three, and then we were, then we just moved on. Until we played Pleasure Beach Park. Over here in Connecticut. And that's what was the last straw on the camel's back. We had three men in the

band that were alchoholic. And these three men couldn't play nothing without their -- and they were, two were trumpet players, and the other was a bass player. And so now, these are very essential in the band. So these fellows couldn't play nothing, and a local band made us look like we're amateurs. Well, that was the -- Albert Alvin Nicholss, he came up and he said, "Well, I'm going to Europe." And Sedric He said, "Well, I'm through." "I'm just going to get in a combination." So later on he went with Fats Waller.
